title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 6th District

context.text: Incumbent James Clyburn (D) won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 90.3% of the vote. John Peterson won the Republican primary with 74.0% of the vote.

candidates.name: James Clyburn

candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 1993); former House Majority Whip (2007-2011, 2019-2023) and Assistant Democratic Leader

summary.text: James Clyburn is the incumbent U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 6th District, seeking re-election. He has served in the House since 1993 and previously held the third-ranking House Democratic leadership position.

background.text: Born in Sumter, South Carolina in 1940. Earned a bachelor's degree in history from South Carolina State College in 1962.

Worked as a teacher, employment counselor, and newspaper publisher, and served on South Carolina state commissions including the State Employment Security Commission and the Human Affairs Commission, before working as a staff member for Gov. John C. West (D).
Elected House Majority Whip for the 116th Congress in 2018, the third-ranking leadership position in the House; served in that role until 2023.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Interior, Environment and Related Agencies subcommittee and the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies subcommittee (2025-2026 assignments).

candidates.name: John Peterson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary (June 9, 2026) with 74.0% of the vote

summary.text: John Peterson is a hotel banquet supervisor and Republican campaign volunteer running as the Republican nominee for South Carolina's 6th Congressional District.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the State University of New York at Brockport.
Works as a banquet supervisor at Embassy Suites in North Charleston, SC. Volunteered as a canvasser and phone caller for Donald Trump's 2020 and 2024 campaigns.

priorities.text: Says he will vote for fiscally conservative bills that cut spending, bring down inflation, and reduce the national debt, and supports the One Subject at a Time Act requiring each bill to cover a single topic.
Supports deregulation and reducing the size of government, including cuts to federal jobs and programs he characterizes as wasteful.
